upstream.distribution: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (git repository, document/ tree)
upstream.revision_basis: Commit at the head of the master branch when the guide was read; the local review copy is byte-identical to document/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing and document/5-Reporting at this commit.
upstream.usage_boundary: Reviewed and, since 2026-10-11, also shipped read-only as on-demand background text: each owning skill's references/wstg-source.md links the unmodified upstream page for its own tests only, behind this library's own bounded-comparison cards, never inlined into a SKILL.md or substituted for a card's controls, stop conditions or evidence fields. No image, tool tutorial or this project's own code depends on the guide at runtime; the condensed cards remain the method this library actually runs. Test identifiers and page titles are used as references.
upstream.attribution: Adapted material is credited by chapter title and a digest of the pages used, and the upstream license text is vendored for conservative attribution. Changes made: condensed, restructured into bounded comparisons with controls and stop conditions, and tools replaced by those the sandbox provides.

adapted: Fingerprint, metafile, page-content and framework identification restated as bounded comparisons against a fixed baseline response set
excluded: Search-engine reconnaissance and DNS or virtual-host enumeration (outside the confirmed origin), tool tutorials, screenshots and sample output

references.document: OWASP WSTG 4.2 Configuration and Deployment Management
adapted: Platform configuration, backup-file, administrative-interface, HTTP-method, HSTS, security-header and feature-flag checks restated with controls, source-review counterparts and stop conditions
Content security policy header review restated as a directive-weakness check against the baseline route set
excluded: Network-infrastructure, cloud-storage and subdomain-takeover tests (other origins), cloud command lines, wordlist enumeration and tool tutorials
Bypass-technique catalogs and JSONP-callback exploitation walkthroughs

adapted: Registration, provisioning and account-enumeration checks restated with throwaway accounts, fixed sample counts and stop conditions
Role-inventory and role-switching checks restated as a comparison between documented permissions and observed reach
excluded: Screenshots of third-party products and tool tutorials

adapted: Browser-cache directive review restated for sensitive authenticated responses
Default-credential, password-rule, lockout, security-question, reset, remember-me and MFA checks restated with counted attempts, operator-controlled mailboxes and stop conditions
excluded: Credential-guessing procedures and tool tutorials; those are handled by cards with their own safeguards
Password lists, credential-stuffing and spraying procedures, and tool tutorials

adapted: Delegated authorization flow checks restated as application-side enforcement of destination matching and one-time value consumption, using a controlled client registration
excluded: Credential-leakage-channel catalogs and identity-provider-specific exploitation walkthroughs

adapted: Token strength, cookie attribute, fixation, exposure, replay, logout, timeout and concurrency checks restated as bounded comparisons with controls, named HTTP sessions and stop conditions
Structured bearer token acceptance checks restated as bounded structural-property changes against a baseline, without the signing key
Cross-site request forgery and request-origin checks restated as a request-bound-token comparison and a SameSite reading, without constructing a live cross-site submission
excluded: Token-prediction tooling and brute-force procedures, forced-cookie attack walkthroughs, tool tutorials, screenshots and sample traffic
Library-specific vulnerability catalogs and tool tutorials
Proof-of-concept HTML form catalogs

adapted: Mass-assignment field-addition checks restated as a one-field-at-a-time comparison against a declared or source-confirmed field allow list
HTTP parameter pollution and response-header injection checks restated as a bounded one-marker comparison between layers, with no connection-desynchronization content
Host and forwarded-host trust checks restated as a one-variable comparison against sinks the application itself reaches, with no cache-poisoning or exploitation walkthrough

Query-language, document-parser, process/template-interpreter, format-call, outbound-request, path-resolution and stored/second-order injection checks restated as bounded, harmless boundary-class comparisons with an inert control, stopping at structural influence rather than exploitation
excluded: Framework-specific binder walkthroughs and payload catalogs
Payload catalogs, intermediary-specific exploitation walkthroughs and tool tutorials
Payload catalogs and intermediary-specific exploitation walkthroughs
Payload catalogs, exploitation walkthroughs, filter-bypass encodings, and any content demonstrating code execution, data exfiltration or denial of service

adapted: Error-output comparison against the stock server error with a small fixed set of malformed requests
excluded: Fuzzing and crash-inducing inputs, and product-specific error catalogs

adapted: TLS configuration facts and clear-channel checks restated around the handshake tools the sandbox provides
Weak-primitive and decryption-error-path checks restated as a source-reading checklist against a fixed weakness list, and a single distinguishability comparison that stops short of key recovery
excluded: Exploit demonstrations of protocol attacks, scanner tutorials and long vulnerability catalogs
Exploit scripts for recovering key material through repeated oracle queries

adapted: Usage-ceiling bypass restated as sequential replay and step re-entry checked first, with the existing two-actor schedule method applied only if the sequential path is sound

Business-logic validation, hidden-field, component-integrity, timing, workflow-order, defense-observation, upload-type-boundary, upload-processing and transaction-recomputation checks restated as named-rule comparisons with inert fixture data, deferring any executable or exploit-demonstrating content to other skills as an open proof gap
excluded: Payment-specific and provider-specific exploitation walkthroughs
Payload catalogs, web-shell and archive-exploitation walkthroughs, and PCI-specific compliance checklists

adapted: CORS, framing, script-loadable-response, WebSocket-origin, client-side sink, messaging, storage and new-tab isolation checks restated as source-to-sink tracing and declared-header comparison, stopping at offline reproduction without a managed browser transport
Client-side template-evaluation checks restated as a plain-text-versus-template-source source trace, stopping at expression evaluation rather than script execution
excluded: DOM-based proof-of-concept payload catalogs and browser-exploitation walkthroughs

adapted: Field-level response-exposure checks restated as a principal-pair diff of serialized fields, extended to list, search and export variants

GraphQL schema-exposure, development-interface and depth/complexity/batch-bound checks restated as a handful of bounded requests, routing field-authorization and resolver-injection questions to the skills that already own them
excluded: GraphQL introspection tooling and client-bundle scraping tutorials
Denial-of-service query construction and resource-exhaustion walkthroughs

adapted: Risk-rating scale and reporting-structure guidance restated as a fixed five-level criteria document bound to existing verdict and review-status gates, never substituting for them
excluded: Report templates, version-control tables, executive-summary boilerplate, and CVSS mapping guidance
